candidates.title: Plan recovery steps for failed agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Developers must write checkpoints and recovery logic and handle idempotency for agent runs.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable recovery checklist for one simulated failed agent run.
experimentPlan.trigger: A developer submits a synthetic run and selects a failure point.
steps: Represent each step and its expected side effect.
Mark the interruption point and proposed checkpoint.
Draft a retry and duplicate-prevention checklist.
Compare the checklist with the expected final state.
Return unresolved decisions for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For the simulated failure, check that the checklist names the expected checkpoint and avoids applying the same side effect twice.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer must define valid state changes, review retry safety, and authorize any production recovery.
unverified: No source documents an implementation reference or existing recovery product.
Production integrations, durable checkpoint storage, and safe replay are unverified.

ease.reason: A beginner can mock one run, but implementing safe replay requires engineering beyond the cited discussion.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agent workflows may pay for recovery help; the post establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic checklist test is possible; durable state and side-effect safety remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed workflow can draft a checklist, but a person must validate state and authorize recovery.

evidence.reason: The discussion explicitly names checkpoints, recovery logic, and idempotency, but gives no frequency or system detail.

candidates.reason: Concrete agent-run recovery work is stated, but the bounded synthetic checklist has no implementation support and the provisional mean is below six.

candidates.title: Summarize email threads for faster review

demandEvidence.chore: Summarize each new email thread into a compact history and prepare draft-prefill context.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: To save email resume properly, i need immutable id to reference original email of the resume.

experimentPlan.output: A compact, source-linked summary of a supplied email thread.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a fictional thread for summarization.
steps: Extract the latest request and relevant prior context.
Draft a concise summary with source-message references.
Check that each detail appears in the input.
Return uncertain references for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare the summary with the supplied messages and confirm every stated detail has a source message reference.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies the thread and boundaries, checks names and meaning, and decides whether to use any draft context.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports email ingestion, immutable identifiers, or draft-prefill integration.
Real email access, privacy review, and summary accuracy are unverified.

ease.reason: A beginner can test summaries on fictional threads, though no implementation reference supports email handling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional teams handling long email threads may pay for review assistance; the post establishes no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week text-only prototype is feasible with synthetic threads; live mailbox access remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed text-to-summary loop is repeatable, but a person must verify context and choose whether to use it.

evidence.reason: The post describes summarizing each new email thread and preparing draft context, but gives limited task detail.

candidates.reason: The author describes a concrete email summarization task. A text-only mock is assessable, but absent integration support and unverified buyer demand keep the provisional mean below six.

candidates.title: Prepare weekly keyword metrics in Sheets

demandEvidence.chore: Collect weekly search volume, CPC, and difficulty for keywords into spreadsheet rows.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Runs VNCNT Labs’ Keyword Search Volume Actor on Apify every week and adds each keyword’s Google search volume, CPC and difficulty as rows in Google Sheets.

experimentPlan.output: A weekly spreadsheet of keyword metrics from operator supplied sample data.
inputs: Sample search volume, CPC, and difficulty values
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a keyword list and sample metric rows.
steps: Match each metric row to its keyword.
Format rows to the supplied spreadsheet columns.
Produce a reviewable weekly sheet export.
Ask a person to verify anomalies before use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare the output rows with a hand-prepared sample and verify every value and keyword match.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies keywords, checks source values, and decides whether the report is suitable for business decisions.
unverified: The source describes an existing Apify actor and workflow, but no implementation reference is attached for a new service.
Live Apify access, account setup, and data reliability are unverified.

ease.reason: A beginner can format supplied sample metrics, but no source supports implementation of the actor workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: SEO consultants may pay for recurring keyword reports; the post does not establish customer demand.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample-data report can be tested; live data access and reliability remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A batch can format rows and flag blanks, but a person must verify data and interpret results.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes weekly keyword volume, CPC, and difficulty rows, though it is one maker workflow.

candidates.reason: A concrete weekly metrics chore is shown, but a new service would lack implementation support and the provisional mean is below six.
